ablations.note: Reopens nothing and changes no case's outcome or reason code in this suite. No attack case reaches the gate with a difference to catch: PayPal rejects every change after authorization (PROTOCOL 4.3), so checks that run before authorization stop every case first. The combined row shows the cases the gate alone stops once the pre-authorize check is also off.
Reopens nothing: 4 case(s) change reason code (payment_failed) but stay blocked. The gate voids the authorization instead (the cases end blocked with payment_failed).
Reopens nothing: 2 case(s) change reason code (unmandated_checkout_not_allowed) but stay blocked. Another check still refuses the unmandated completes, with a different reason code.

Reopens nothing: 1 case(s) change reason code (http_404) but stay blocked. The only case it touches is the webhook spoof, which is refused because no webhook endpoint is mounted without reconciliation; no case drives the budget through PayPal-side state.
Reopens nothing: 2 case(s) change reason code (http_201, invalid_field) but stay blocked. The lenient parser accepts the body, and the field validation downstream still refuses it.
Both layers off at once (not an architecture ablation): reopens the listed attacks.

caveats: The adversary is scripted: 12 fixed goals per seed, each re-performing one attack case. No model plans an attack, so there is no attack success rate with a confidence interval, and no claim about an adaptive attacker (L65).

The baseline gap is 11 of 40 cases. The other cases are blocked in baseline too (defense in depth in the careful baseline), so the cases widen coverage without widening the gap between the modes (L67).
Latency is simulator latency. The PayPal simulator answers in memory, so the gate's added time is its own computation and database work, not PayPal round trips.
The legitimate tasks run through the test issuer and the PayPal simulator, not the model-driven shopper or live PayPal. The completion rate is for those fixed purchases.
Seeds change only the Hypothesis examples. The attack, adversary and task suites have no randomness, so three seeds are three repetitions, not three samples of a distribution.
Ground truth is simulator state. The simulator is our model of PayPal; agreement with live PayPal is established by the recorded cassettes and the sandbox smoke script, not by this report.

Nothing here is a claim about PayPal buyer or seller protection or dispute outcomes. The evidence bundles are verified for internal consistency and signatures, not for how any dispute would be decided.
Passing counts are counts of passing tests under a seed, not of Hypothesis examples.
